item.content:encoded:
This is really great, subtly taking something which the assumed audience would be familiar with and presenting it in a really eerie, alarming fashion. Some powerful primal fear material here. Also, for some reason the oven being the access point is one of the clinchers for me - it's one of those details that is perfect for hard-to-explain reasons.

It reminds me very strongly of Jeffrey Allen Manchester (an escaped prisoner who hid in the wall of a Toys 'R Us for 2 months, stealing baby food and watching the store through stolen nanny cams). IIRC (based entirely on the account of it in The Burglar's Guide to the City by Geoff Manaugh) he had actually drawn up rough plans for his 'dream house', which was so thoroughly riddled with secret passageways that he could watch every part of it without being seen.

item.content:encoded: You didn't give this scp a name in the mainlist for series 1

The prospect of having something observing and taking photos of you in your own home (with no restrictions) does allude towards the classic stalker approach in a pretty interesting way. The obsessive tendencies towards recording past residents of this area does also give some leeway for expansion of Tales, which is also pretty neato.

The linear progression of the article itself does drive the point across in a concise manner. I think, in this circumstance, its a beneficial approach for the article itself.

Good job
